verdict_scope: the mark's own instrument: the PR bench, unchanged, eager launches, new r1 boots against the 1107 arm of the candidate-49 own-mark receipts (two boots), as instructed. By kernel time (CUPTI) and by CUDA-graph replay of the same 45 cases, no cell is slower and every cell is faster beyond its two-boot interval.
reason: The defensible correction is in the GEMM epilogue: the PR forced its row loop rolled (#pragma unroll 1), which left the decode GEMM at M=1..4 with no gain (kernel time PR 5.120 us vs 1107 5.120-5.184 us); r1 keeps 1107's T.serial loop, which nvcc unrolls, and the decode GEMM is 3.7-5.1% faster at every M (CUPTI kernel time; 3.7-4.8% in graph replay), and the M=1 cell is now a gain beyond the interval in the bench. The paged-key 'slowdowns' at M=2/4/6/2048 were never kernel slowdowns (kernel time 30-57% lower at every M); those eager cells sit on the host launch path (~3.9 us/launch against 1.2-2.6 us of kernel), and with r1 they read as gains or within. The mark is still missed: GEMM M=6 and M=8 measure slower beyond the interval in all three r1 bench boots (6.36-6.52 us vs 1107's 6.198/5.833 and 6.116/5.874). There the faster kernel drops the bench's loop of identical eager launches out of its queued mode (in-run paired +4..+12%, and 5.53/5.54 us, faster than 1107, in one companion boot), while kernel time and graph replay show r1 4.6-5.1% faster at the same M. With the clean boot pair (1 and 3), paged keys M=1 is also flagged: both arms ran at 10-11.6 us in that first cell (paired -0.5/+2.7%). The query-rope M=2048 gain is not claimed: it reads +1.3/+5.6% in the receipts and -8.7% to -30% here.

change_vs_0764: gemm.py: mxfp8_gemm_rope_mxfp4_decode's epilogue row loop back to 1107's T.serial(iters) (drops the PR's T.unroll(..., pragma_unroll_factor=1)); comment states why
test_deepseek_v41_tilelang_linear.py: test_hw_e2m1x2_codegen_in_gemm_and_indexer_quantizers also asserts the GEMM source has no '#pragma unroll 1'
commit message: rationale, measured kernel times, test line updated; the 'loop rolled' claim and the static-SASS framing dropped
indexer.py, test_deepseek_v4_1_lsa.py and the E2M1 helpers: unchanged from 0764
patch.applies: exactly on 1107 + 0762 + 0763 (the four files reconstructed from the image by reversing 0764; blob hashes match 0764's index lines); also on 1107 alone (indexer.py hunks at offset -165). 0765..0767 touch none of the four files. git diff --check clean.

cause.gemm_M1: PR's '#pragma unroll 1' on the 4-row epilogue loop (block_M=16, 256 threads, 4 rows per pass). Rolled, each pass runs the loop counter and five pointer/row increments, the compare and back-edge plus a BSSY/BSYNC region (diag/dump/gemm_pr_bm16.sass, 0x1840-0x18b0); unrolled, nvcc folds the row offsets into immediates (STG [R2.64+0x2000/0x4000/0x6000]) and exits after the last row check (gemm_hw_serial_bm16.sass). The GEMM main loop is the same SASS in both. Kernel time (CUPTI, isolated launches, 300 each): 1107 5.152/5.120/5.184 us at M=1/2/4, PR 5.120/5.120/5.120, unrolled 4.928/4.928/4.960 (diag/cupti-1.json). So the hardware conversion alone saved ~0 at M<=4, where 1 to 4 of 16 rows are live, and the eager bench's +/-1% noise decided the sign of the M=1 cell. The unrolled body is larger (static SASS 720 vs 440 at bm16); static count is not the cost. At block_M=32 and 64 rolled and unrolled are within 0.03 us (CUPTI) / 0.1 us (graph).
cause.paged_keys_small_M_and_2048: Not a kernel regression. Kernel time 1107 -> PR/r1: 1.952 -> 1.216 us (M=1), 1.984 -> 1.248 (M=2,4), 2.080 -> 1.312 (M=6), 3.904 -> 2.624 (M=2048). The PR bench times 25 (or 5) back-to-back eager TileLang launches per sample; for this 3-argument kernel that path costs ~3.9 us per launch (and ~4.7 us per sample at 5 launches), above either kernel's time, so both arms read the launch floor and the hw arm's +1..+6% in the receipts is launch-path jitter: today the same unchanged PR measured -0.3..-1.1% at M=2..6 and -2.5% at 2048 (diag/bench-pr-asis.json), and r1 boots 1 and 2 read -0.1..-0.4% and -2.3/-2.1% (boot 3 +1.9..+2.4% at M=2..6, inside a slow first phase where both arms ran at ~11 us; -2.4% at 2048). Register pressure is not involved (52 -> 43 registers).
cause.gemm_M6_M8_in_r1: Eager-launch bistability, not kernel time. The GEMM's launch path costs ~6.2-6.5 us per eager launch; 1107's kernel at M=6/8 (5.4-5.6 us) keeps the launch queue fed and reads ~5.7-5.8 us; r1's (5.2-5.3 us) usually drains it and reads the launch cost, 6.36-6.52 us, but read 5.53/5.54 us in the first companion boot. At M=1..4 every variant reads the launch cost (~6.2-6.5 us) with q75 up to 10-12 us. Inference from these numbers; not traced at the driver level.
cause.query_rope_M2048: Not reproducible as a stable claim. 16 MiB in + 4 MiB out per call; memory-bound with large run-to-run spread (receipts +1.3/+5.6%; today PR as is -23.6% and -8.1%; r1 -21.2/-30.4/-8.7% paired; graph 1.23x). Not claimed.
cause.serving_note: Decode runs these kernels from CUDA graphs (pdl.py: 'A decode step is one chain of about 1,850 small kernels in CUDA graphs'), where the launch path is off the critical path; the plain paged-key writer (write_index_keys) is reached only when positions is None, and attention.py always passes positions, so serving writes index keys through mxfp4_norm_rope_quantize_v41.

They are not claimed.
First-cell-after-compile slow phases hit both arms in every session: receipts query RoPE M=1 boot2 12.43 us; r1 paged keys M=1 10.25 (boot1) and M=1..8 11.1-11.6 (boot3); norm-RoPE M=1 13.9 (boot2).

Claims kept for r1 (bench, beyond the interval vs 1107 receipts, boots 1 and 3): GEMM M=1 1.017x, M=16 1.065x, M=32 1.057x, M=64 1.062x; query RoPE M=512 1.556x; paged keys M=8192 2.067x; norm-RoPE shards1 M=8192 1.204x.
